title: Epoll vs. io_uring in Linux
summary: A technical comparison of two Linux kernel I/O mechanisms - the traditional epoll interface and the newer io_uring system. The article explores their differences in performance, design philosophy, and use cases for building high-performance I/O-bound applications on Linux.
problem_solved: Helps developers choose between epoll and io_uring for building high-performance Linux applications with optimal I/O handling.
why_valuable: Both interfaces are fundamental to building modern high-performance servers and network applications on Linux, and understanding their trade-offs is critical for optimizing I/O-intensive workloads.
